checkedAlternates.risk: Food is usually oiled before it goes on a grill.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The heat travels by fire and radiant heat, not through oil; the oil is a coating.

checkedAlternates.risk: A wok gets extremely hot, which can read as dry heat.
checkedAlternates.resolution: Stir-frying always has oil in the pan, and it is the oil that carries the heat to the food.

checkedAlternates.risk: Roasting a joint or vegetables normally involves oil in the tray.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The oven air does the cooking; the same food roasts without oil.

checkedAlternates.risk: A microwave heats the water inside the food, so it can read as water-based.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The carrier is the microwave radiation; that water is the food’s own, not a cooking medium.

authorReview.notes: The hardest of the ten. Every method involves some oil or some water in practice, so the rule is which one carries the heat, and the explanation says so directly.

blindPlaytest.notes: If testers cannot recover the rule from the groups, move this family later in the schedule and lead with an easier one.
